# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 89 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 50 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_089_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 89

**1** Jesus said: "Why do you wash the outside of the cup?

**2** Do you not understand that he who made the inside is also he who made the outside?"

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**Text:** Thomas's cup-washing saying (cf. Matt 23:25-26; Luke 11:39-40) strips the Synoptic moral condemnation and focuses on a creator-unity argument: the same maker made both inside and outside.

**"He who made"** — preserved (EMET) — the personal maker language is important; PNEUMA's "whoever" is too neutral.

**Theological Note:** This transforms the saying from an anti-Pharisee polemic into a cosmological statement: you cannot treat the inside and outside as belonging to different creators. This may be a subtle anti-Gnostic or anti-Marcionite point: the material outside is not made by a lesser demiurge; the same creator made both.

**Synoptic Parallels:** Matt 23:25-26; Luke 11:39-40. Thomas removes the polemical framing and the moral exhortation ("first clean the inside"), leaving only the ontological question.
